mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.25%, market expectations for future discount rates fall, lowering the present value of future dividends and driving a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: FOMC holds rates steady in a restrictive regime
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day average during similar non-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening in early expansion phase
failure_condition: During analogous labor-market tightening episodes, the same cross-series pattern does not produce a statistically significant positive 20-day forward return (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) of at least 3% for three consecutive months predicts a temporary boost in investor sentiment and equity pricing, resulting in a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During analogous demand expansions, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month coincides with elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4.0%), signaling supply-side stress that raises risk premia and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% AND CPIAUCSL > 4.0 in the same month
failure_condition: In analogous supply shocks, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.5% for two consecutive months, without a corresponding cut in the federal funds rate, suggests the Fed is not tightening, lowering real interest rates and supporting equity valuations, which predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.5 for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS ≥ 5.0 for the same months
failure_condition: During analogous low-inflation holds, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in job openings (RSAFS) exceeding 1.5 million for a month while unemployment remains below 3.5% indicates a tight labor market, which can fuel wage growth and equity optimism, producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 1.5 million AND UNRATE < 3.5 in the same month
failure_condition: In analogous tight labor markets, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in consumer confidence (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual: a sharp drop in GDP deflator inflation proxy CPIAUCSL combined with a simultaneous rise in retail sales HOUST of >5% suggests demand softening, which predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by >2% AND HOUST increases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: During analogous demand weakening, the 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS above 6% triggers a sharp rise in real risk-free rates, compressing equity present value and producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During analogous high-rate periods, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).
